evaluation.results_summary: The developer reports that AceMath-7B-RM achieves an average score of 67.41 across the listed math reasoning benchmarks, with the highest score on GSM8K at 96.66 and the lowest on Minerva Math at 41.96.

identity.name: AceMath-7B-RM
identity.summary: AceMath-7B-RM is a member of the AceMath family of math reasoning models, released as an open-weight reward model for evaluating mathematical solutions.

possible_risks.description: Copyrighted information or other intellectual property might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
possible_risks.justification: open-weight reward model with cc-by-nc-4.0 license and no stated guardrails; users can submit math problems containing copyrighted text, and the model processes the prompt as text.

possible_risks.description: Confidential information might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
possible_risks.justification: open-weight text-in/text-out reward model with no stated data-handling safeguards; users may include confidential math or proprietary problem statements in prompts.

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: reward model evaluated on math reasoning benchmarks with low scores on Minerva Math (41.96), indicating it can produce or score incorrect mathematical content.

possible_risks.description: In AI-assisted decision-making tasks, reliance measures how much a person trusts (and potentially acts on) a model's output. Over-reliance occurs when a person puts too much trust in a model, accepting a model's output when the model's output is likely incorrect. Under-reliance is the opposite, where the person doesn't trust the model but should.
possible_risks.justification: reported as a reward model for evaluating mathematical solutions, so downstream users may rely on its scores despite uneven benchmark performance (e.g., 41.96 on Minerva Math).

specifications.model_size: 13.2 GiB of safetensors weights (14,141,284,264 bytes) in BF16
